Posted on 11 May 2026
Activity and Creativity Days 2026
We are excited to launch our Activity and Creativity Days 2026 for students in Years 7–9. These will take place at the end of Term 6: Monday 20th – Tuesday 21st July: Two-day activity Wednesday 22nd July: Half-day in school celebrating students’ experiences Students will take part in one two-day activity, giving them the chance to try something new, build confidence and enjoy time with their peers. We’ve designed a wide range of activities to inspire creativity, teamwork and a sense of achievement. You can find full details of all activities in the booklet here: ACTIVITY AND CREATIVITY DAYS BOOKLET Each activity includes information about which year group it is for, what to bring and approximate costs involved. A couple of quick updates: The Year 9 residential (Deers Leap) is now full. There are still some places available on the Eastbourne water sports trip for Years 8 and 9. Supporting all students We know that trips and activities can be a financial pressure for some families. Students eligible for free school meals or pupil premium will receive up to £50 towards costs, automatically applied in Arbor. If you would like to request support or a flexible payment plan, please contact: trips@priory.e-sussex.sch.uk We are also offering a voluntary “Pay it Forward” option via Arbor, where families can contribute towards another student’s place if they wish. This is entirely optional but greatly appreciated. What you need to do now Talk through the options in the booklet with your child. Submit their choices (one first choice and two reserves) by Monday 18th May @10pm using this form: Activity and Creativity Days: Monday 20th and Tuesday 21st July 2026 – Fill out form If no form is submitted, a free activity will be allocated. Check that consent forms on Arbor are completed, as we can’t take students on activities without these. Once all forms have been received, we will send a follow-up letter to confirm your child’s activity and payment via Arbor. We’ll finish the week with a celebration of all the students’ experiences and achievements on Wednesday. If you have any questions or would like help choosing, please don’t hesitate to get in touch: info@priory.e-sussex.sch.uk Thank you, as always, for your support—we hope students have a fantastic and memorable experience!
Posted on 11 May 2026
Follow Us on Instagram for School Updates
Want to keep up to date with life at Priory School? Our Instagram page is the best place to see what’s happening across the school day-to-day. We regularly share: Key school updates and reminders Celebrations of student achievements Trips, events and enrichment activities Assemblies, performances and sporting highlights Important notices and whole-school moments Following us is a great way to stay connected and get a real glimpse into school life as it happens. You can find us on Instagram by searching @PriorySchoolLewes We’d love to have you following along!
Posted on 14 Apr 2026
Spring Summer Menu out now!
We’re excited to share our brand-new Spring/Summer 2026 menu, now being served in school! Students can enjoy a wide range of fresh, tasty and nutritious options each day – from hot favourites and street-food inspired dishes to vegetarian and vegan choices. You can view the full menu here.

Posted on 2 Mar 2026
World Book Day 2026
We look forward to celebrating World Book Day on Thursday 5th March. This is always a much‑loved event in our school calendar and a wonderful opportunity for our whole community to come together to celebrate the joy of books and reading. This year’s event ties into the National Year of Reading, the biggest UK reading campaign in a generation. It was launched in response to worrying declines in young people reading for pleasure. The theme, “Go All In – If you're into it, read into it,” encourages children to discover books that match their interests - from sport and music to fashion, gaming, animals, adventures, and anything else that sparks their curiosity. One of the highlights of the day will be our book-themed costume competition. Students and staff are invited to come dressed as a favourite book character - whether from a classic novel, a modern story, a poem, a picture book, or a graphic novel. Costumes can be as simple or as imaginative as students wish. If possible, we encourage pupils to bring the book itself, or a printed copy of the cover, so they can share the story behind their costume.

pageCache.text:
Lewes Co-operative Learning Partnership
The Lewes Cooperative Learning Partnership (LCLP) was established in 2014 as a charitable trust with a founding intention to improve the learning outcomes for all Lewes pupils, enhance the effectiveness of all our teaching professionals and deliver a broader range of opportunities for parents and other stakeholders to contribute to the success of our local education services.
The two foundation schools Priory Secondary School and Western Road Primary School were joined by other Partner Schools: Iford and Kingston Primary School, South Malling Primary School and Southover Primary School. The trust Board comprises trustees appointed by the Foundation and Partner Schools with their headteachers automatically holding trustee status.
Trust funding is derived from participating school subscriptions and it holds three Board meetings per year alongside an Annual General Meeting. Other work is conducted by members of occasional working parties nominated by trustees. The trust works closely with the Lewes headteachers’ forum and the Education Improvement Partnership (EIP).
Enquiries to the LCLP can be made to: lclp@priory.e-sussex.sch.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher's Welcome - Welcome to Priory School Lewes
pageCache.text:
Headteacher's Welcome
On behalf of the students, staff and governors, a very warm welcome to Priory School.
We are a thriving 11–16 mixed comprehensive school at the heart of our community in Lewes.
Priory School has a proud tradition of providing a rich, well-rounded education. Our students benefit from a long-established record of academic excellence, supported by a culture of strong pastoral care that ensures every young person feels known, valued, and supported.
We set high expectations for all our students, encouraging them to work hard, aim high, and take pride in their progress. At the same time, we place equal importance on wellbeing, belonging, and personal development. Our broad and balanced curriculum reflects the diverse community we serve, and our reputation for quality means we are consistently oversubscribed.
Our ambition is for Priory to be the region’s leading inclusive and creative state secondary school—one where every student gains powerful knowledge, develops a deep sense of connection and belonging, and grows into an ethically aware young adult ready to contribute confidently to the world.
We are equally committed to celebrating the unique character of Lewes, both its history and its vibrant social fabric.
Thank you for taking the time to learn more about Priory School. We look forward to welcoming you into our community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Information & Guidance - Welcome to Priory School Lewes
pageCache.text:
Careers Information & Guidance
CEIAG (Careers Education, Information, Advice and Guidance) is designed to prepare students by providing the knowledge, understanding, confidence and skills that they need to make informed choices and plans for their future learning and career.
Every student at Priory School is entitled to receive independent and impartial careers information, advice and guidance. Our CEIAG programme provides activities appropriate to age and need; it aims to provide students with the best possible foundation on which to base not only their post-16 choices following Year 11, but also their Key Stage 4 option choices in Year 9. Please click here for the CEIAG Strategic Action Plan.
We believe that all our students have the power and potential to grow in their careers. Excellent careers guidance makes sure there is equality of opportunity. The Career programme at Priory School is therefore designed to support students throughout the stages of their journey and build their career development learning skills, which are acquired alongside academic and vocational pursuits. These can be developed through specific careers activities, within the curriculum (both through other subjects and discrete time for careers education) and during enrichment and extracurricular activities, as well as through personal guidance.
Priory knows that every student’s needs are different, therefore from Year 7 onwards we prepare students for a variety of pathways: technical, vocational, and the academic. The school has a distributed leadership approach to Careers guidance. Roles are spread out across Senior Leaders and Support Staff.

pageCache.pageTitle: Arts, Culture & Creativity - Welcome to Priory School Lewes
pageCache.text:
Arts, Culture & Creativity
At Priory, we are proud to champion the arts as a core part of our identity and vision.
We actively encourage students to see themselves as musicians, artists, actors, writers, dancers, and filmmakers of the future. Through initiatives like our Student Arts Leaders panel, creative careers events, and work experience opportunities, we aim to open doors into the vibrant world of the creative industries.
Our School Plan places arts and culture at its heart—supporting academic excellence, creative expression, student wellbeing, and staff development. We believe every student deserves access to a rich and inspiring creative education.
Some of our recent projects, programmes and partnerships:
As of 2024 Priory now has a 5-hour/week position of Arts, Culture and Creativity Co-ordinator, Ms Brooke-Smith and Priory's Headteacher, Mr Curtis-Brignell is a Leader for Impact (awarded by Royal Ballet and Opera and supported by Arts Council England)
There is a CPD working group of visual and performing arts staff that meet throughout the school year
Annual whole cohort trip to Glyndebourne for all Year 7 students, subsidised tickets and free for students in receipt of Pupil Premium
Schools partner with Charleston Trust for artist-led workshops, exhibition opportunities and work experience
Student Leaders for Arts, Culture and Creativity
Careers in the Creative Industries Fair
Elderflower Fields Festival exhibition opportunity and work experience
Dance performance opportunities, for example Let’s Dance, The Old Market, Trinity Laban
Dance and drama workshops with professional companies and practitioners such as Complicite
Regular drama trips to London and Brighton theatres
National Poetry By Heart competition
School drama production
Music trips to Glyndebourne and Barbican
Anti-bullying creative writing project with Lewes Football Club and University of Sussex
Patina art workshops with feeder primary school and Priory samba band
Priory Ruin student-led newspaper
Resident student-led magazine
Art Wave exhibition in Lewes
Farley Arts Trust competition
Outreach workshops with our Lewes feeder primary schools
After school clubs including; Creative Writing, Art, Dance, Drama and Music clubs
Staff and student photography competitions

BFI Into Film Club programmed by Student Arts and Creativity Leaders

pageCache.pageTitle: Remote Learning - Welcome to Priory School Lewes
pageCache.text:
Remote Learning
Priory School has always strived to be creative and innovative, and to support our students, parents, and carers in the most appropriate ways in order to make learning purposeful and engaging. Our strategy for remote learning is in keeping with this philosophy:
• ensure consistency in the approach to remote learning for all students (inc. SEND) who are not in school, through the use of quality online and offline resources and teaching videos. • provide clear expectations to members of the school community with regards to the delivery of high quality interactive remote learning. • maintain continuous delivery of the school curriculum, as well as support for motivation, health and wellbeing, and parents/carers. • consider continued development for staff and parents/carers (e.g., CPD, online resources).
We take a blended approach to providing remote learning. Resources to deliver this Remote Learning include: • Online tools: EduLink; Microsoft Teams; School Website. • Use of instructional videos which are recorded asynchronously. • Phone calls from school to home for students of concern. • Printed learning packs are sent home for students who do not have access to a computer and/or internet. • Physical materials such as writing tools and laptops for students needing support in this regard. • Lessons delivered live via Teams as part of a remote lessons timetable.
Priory School is committed to working in close partnership with families and recognises that each family is unique. Because of this, remote learning will look different for different families in order to suit their individual needs.

pageCache.pageTitle: Special Educational Needs & Disabilities - Welcome to Priory School Lewes
pageCache.text:
Special Educational Needs & Disabilities
At Priory, the principle of inclusion shapes our comprehensive approach to Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND).
We believe that all young people, regardless of their individual circumstances, can achieve personal excellence and should receive the necessary support to do so. To support students with SEND, we implement a focused curriculum, effective interventions and therapies, and high-quality teaching by skilled staff. This enables all students with SEND to learn, progress, and benefit from the structured steps we have established.
We promote a collaborative environment where a team surrounds each student with SEND, encouraging cooperation among individuals, their parents or carers, and staff to enhance the educational experience and improve life opportunities during their time at our school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Activities & Creativity Days 2026 - Welcome to Priory School Lewes
pageCache.text:
Activities & Creativity Days 2026
Priory School is excited to launch our Activity and Creativity Days 2026 for students in Years 7–9.
These will take place at the end of Term 6:
Monday 20th – Tuesday 21st July: Two-day activity
Wednesday 22nd July: Half-day in school celebrating students’ experiences
Students will take part in one two-day activity, giving them the chance to try something new, build confidence and enjoy time with their peers. We’ve designed a wide range of activities to inspire creativity, teamwork and a sense of achievement.
You can find full details of all activities in the booklet here: ACTIVITY AND CREATIVITY DAYS BOOKLET
Each activity includes information about which year group it is for, what to bring and approximate costs involved.
A couple of quick updates:
The Year 9 residential (Deers Leap) is now full.
There are still some places available on the Eastbourne water sports trip for Years 8 and 9.
Supporting all students
We know that trips and activities can be a financial pressure for some families.
Students eligible for free school meals or pupil premium will receive up to £50 towards costs, automatically applied in Arbor.
If you would like to request support or a flexible payment plan, please contact: trips@priory.e-sussex.sch.uk
We are also offering a voluntary “Pay it Forward” option via Arbor, where families can contribute towards another student’s place if they wish. This is entirely optional but greatly appreciated.
What you need to do now
Talk through the options in the booklet with your child.
Submit their choices (one first choice and two reserves) by Monday 18th May @10pm using this form: Activity and Creativity Days: Monday 20th and Tuesday 21st July 2026 – Fill out form If no form is submitted, a free activity will be allocated.
Check that consent forms on Arbor are completed, as we can’t take students on activities without these.
Once all forms have been received, we will send a follow-up letter to confirm your child’s activity and payment via Arbor.
We’ll finish the week with a celebration of all the students’ experiences and achievements on Wednesday.
If you have any questions or would like help choosing, please don’t hesitate to get in touch: info@priory.e-sussex.sch.uk
